title: s-block elements
group: CHEM-ATOM / CHEM-PER — Atoms & the Periodic Table
examples: What makes the alkali metals so reactive?
Can you explain why lithium is different from other alkali metals?
How do the properties change down Group 1?

explain.say: Today we look at the s-block elements on the periodic table.
Alkali metals in Group one are very reactive metals.
Alkaline earth metals in Group two are also reactive.
Lithium and beryllium show some unusual properties.
The smaller size of lithium gives it unique chemical behaviour.
In reality, these metals react with water to produce hydrogen gas.

faq.q: Why are alkali metals so reactive?
faq.a: They have only one valence electron in their outermost shell. Losing this single electron is very easy for them.
asks: What makes Group 1 elements so reactive?

faq.q: How does the reactivity change down Group 1?
faq.a: Reactivity increases down the group because the outermost electron is further from the nucleus and easier to remove.
asks: Is potassium more reactive than lithium?
Does reactivity increase or decrease down the group?

faq.q: What is the difference between Group 1 and Group 2 metals?
faq.a: Group 1 metals lose one electron to form a +1 ion, while Group 2 metals lose two electrons to form a +2 ion.
asks: What charge do Group 2 elements form?

faq.a: Lithium is small enough that its electronic configuration causes it to show properties different from the rest of the group.
asks: Is lithium special among the alkali metals?
What is anomalous behaviour in chemistry?

faq.q: Do all s-block elements react with water?
faq.a: Most reactive ones do, but the reaction rate depends on the specific metal and temperature used.
asks: What conditions are needed for reaction?

facts: Alkali metals belong to Group 1 of the periodic table.
Alkaline earth metals belong to Group 2.
Group 1 elements typically form ions with a +1 charge.
The reactivity of Group 1 metals increases down the group.

quiz.say: Which group contains elements that tend to lose two valence electrons?
quiz.why: Group 2 elements have two valence electrons, making it energetically favorable to lose both and form a +2 ion.

wrong.0: Group 17 elements are halogens and tend to gain electrons, not lose them.
wrong.1: Group 0 elements are generally unreactive noble gases.
wrong.3: Group 1 elements only have one valence electron, so they form +1 ions.

quiz.say: If a metal forms a stable ion with a charge of +1, it is most likely from which group?
quiz.why: Losing one electron results in a +1 charge, which is characteristic of Group 1 alkali metals.

wrong.0: Group 13 elements usually lose three electrons to form a +3 ion.
wrong.2: Group 2 elements typically lose two electrons to form a +2 ion.
wrong.3: Group 18 elements are stable and do not readily form ions.

quiz.say: Which statement best describes the reactivity trend for Group 1 metals?

options.show: Reactivity increases as you go down the group.
options.say: Reactivity increases as you go down the group.

options.show: Reactivity decreases as you go down the group.
options.say: Reactivity decreases as you go down the group.

options.show: Reactivity is constant across the group.
options.say: Reactivity is constant across the group.

options.show: Reactivity depends only on the element's mass.
options.say: Reactivity depends only on the element's mass.

quiz.why: As you move down the group, the valence electron is further from the nucleus, making it easier to remove.

wrong.1: This suggests the outer electron is held more tightly, which is incorrect.
wrong.2: The distance from the nucleus changes, affecting electron removal energy.
wrong.3: Reactivity is determined by electronic structure, not just physical mass.
